feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 9 (base_speed 1.2, kd 0.5, 412.7) confirmed that the bends were limited by control, not geometry: the oval finished 20 of 20, the slalom line loss fell from 3.0 to 2.1, and the bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.37. The mass change in iteration 8 (303.6) and the controller change in iteration 9 are the two gains so far, and all geometry levers tried earlier (span 40 to 60 mm, forward position 0.04 to 0.075 m, footprint 12 and 16 mm, track 0.10 and 0.12 m) either left bend line loss at 2.0 or cost oval finishes. I am holding your iteration-9 geometry unchanged for this race, as you asked, so that the controller result reads cleanly. Your condition for the exploratory track change is the right one, but it can only be judged after this race: if the s-bend line_loss_events is still 2.0 or more and the oval finish rate holds near 1.0, then wheel_track 0.14 m is the next geometry test, since 0.10 m (iteration 7) was the only track width tried and it lost the oval finishes. Keep the five sensors at y = 0.075 m with the 50 mm span, because that layout has the best oval results. Keep body_width at 0.12 m, since the off-track limit is already at its 0.06 m floor.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-9 geometry for this race and change only the controller, as proposed. If the s-bend line_loss_events falls below 2.3 with the oval finish rate at or above 0.9, keep the geometry and move the controller further in the same direction.

If the s-bend or slalom line_loss_events stays at 2.0 or more after this controller change, test wheel_track 0.14 m as the single geometry change in the next iteration, since 0.10 m is the only narrower track tried and it lost the oval finishes.

Keep the five sensors at y = 0.075 m with x = plus or minus 0.025 m and the 12 mm footprint. Widening the span to 60 mm, the 16 mm footprint and the 0.10 m track each cost oval finishes, so do not revisit them.
